children: Key Takeaways
Harmonic's cOS™ virtualized platform enables Lightcurve to deliver up to 8 Gbps downstream and 1 Gbps upstream to MDUs over existing coax infrastructure.
Reusing in-building wiring, Lightcurve can offer competitive speeds without the cost of fiber overbuild.
The virtualized access architecture supports multi-gigabit speeds over DOCSIS while preserving optionality for fiber in the future.
SAN JOSE, Calif., Sept. 24, 2026 /PRNewswire/ --
) today announced that broadband service provider

, serving communities across central and western Washington state, is delivering multi-gigabit services to Multi-Dwelling Units (MDUs) over existing coax wiring using Harmonic's cOS™ virtualized broadband platform. The Harmonic solution enables Lightcurve to offer fiber-like speeds of up to 8 Gbps downstream and 1 Gbps upstream without replacing the buildings' existing coax wiring. This approach helps Lightcurve strengthen its competitive market positioning and meet subscriber demand for higher speeds while maximizing the value of its network investments.

"By pairing Harmonic's Oyster solution with cOS and with the coax infrastructure already in place in the communities we serve, we're able to bring multi-gigabit speeds to our MDU customers quickly and cost-effectively, while keeping the door open to fiber as our network continues to evolve," said Dr. Pao Lo, COO at Lightcurve. "It's the kind of practical, forward-looking approach our subscribers in Washington state have come to expect from Lightcurve."

Lightcurve is advancing its multi-gigabit broadband service strategy through a swift, efficient software upgrade of the cOS Core combined with the deployment of Harmonic's compact low-power Oyster nodes equipped with Pebble Remote PHY devices in a distributed access architecture (DAA). The cOS virtualized platform supports both DOCSIS and fiber, giving the operator the optionality to evolve its network as customer demand and investment priorities shift.

Lightcurve is also using Harmonic's Central AI-driven network intelligence and operations to gain continuous network analytics and visibility. This enables Lightcurve to proactively identify and troubleshoot service issues, supporting a consistent subscriber experience.

"Lightcurve's network strategy is a solid example of how operators can deliver true fiber-like performance without the time, cost and disruption of a fiber overbuild," said Jeffrey Glahn, Senior Vice President of Global Sales at Harmonic. "With our open cOS platform, Lightcurve can unlock multi-gigabit speeds over its existing coax infrastructure while preserving full optionality to bring fiber to the network on its own timeline. This is exactly the flexible, capital-efficient path to multi-gigabit broadband that many operators need today."

Harmonic is the market share leader in cable broadband equipment, virtual CMTS and DAA, according to Dell'Oro Group, the trusted source for market information about the telecommunications, networks and data center IT industries. The company's market-leading cOS virtualized broadband platform powers next-gen broadband services through more than 48 million CPE devices worldwide for leading operators in North America, Europe, Latin America and Asia. To learn more about Harmonic's broadband solutions, visit www.harmonicinc.com.
